key_insight: The paper reframes photon subtraction as Gaussian blurring/filtering in Wigner space, revealing how squeezing, measurement, and loss can be traded off to better design near-deterministic non-Gaussian state sources.
engineering_relevance: This gives a practical optimization framework for continuous-variable quantum hardware, helping engineers balance success rate, feed-forward compatibility, and loss tolerance when generating cat, cubic phase, and GKP states.
method: Introduce a Gaussian-blur-and-filter formalism for measured Fock Wigner functions.
Show that squeezing, Gaussian measurements, and photon loss contribute to the same effective blur and can be interchanged in protocol design.
Use the framework to derive improved and hybrid photon-subtraction setups, plus a lower bound based on expected Wigner logarithmic negativity.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports analytical improvements and resource bounds for multiple target-state generation scenarios, but does not mention experimental data or numerical benchmarks.
watch_item: The proposed gains may depend on carefully managing loss and feed-forward constraints, so hardware imperfections could limit how much of the theoretical improvement is realized.
paper_title: General Photon Subtraction from a Gaussian Perspective
